submitted.rationale: Of three measured compositions, the most Sb-rich one (Sb 0.81) gave the highest EQE, 0.0055%. That is about 8x the MgSb2O6 composition and about 37x the 1:1 composition. Its XRD shows extra peaks beyond the MgSb2O6-region pattern, suggesting Sb-rich oxide phases with smaller predicted gaps that can absorb 2.7 eV light.

rejected.reason: MgSb2O6 stoichiometry (predicted gap 2.8 eV, on hull), but measured EQE was only 0.0007%
MgO, Mg3SbO4 and Mg4Sb2O9 have predicted gaps of 3.1-4.2 eV, above the 2.7 eV photon energy

consultations.verdict: Support: MgSb2O6 (mp-3653) is on hull (MACE) with HSE gap 2.82 eV, closest to 2.7 eV illumination; Mg-rich phases have wider gaps (3.1-4.2 eV). Index 24 matches MgSb2O6 stoichiometry.

Weak support: Sb-rich Mg-Sb oxides (MgSb4O9, MgSb3O7) are predicted to have small gaps (0.04-0.7 eV), and Sb2O4 1.7 eV, so they absorb at 2.7 eV. MgSb2O6 composition gave near-zero EQE, so explore the Sb-rich end, whose XRD shows extra phase peaks.

Moderate support: MgSbO3 (Mg:Sb 1:1, matching index 18) has a predicted HSE gap of 1.2 eV, so it absorbs at 2.7 eV, and this mid-line region has not been sampled yet. The Mg-rich phases have gaps of 3.1-4.2 eV, which argues against measuring the Mg end.
